title: The Renaissance

cards.h: A bank, a family and a dome that should not have stood
cards.b:
In 1418, Florence announced a contest. The great cathedral had a huge gap in its roof, wider than anyone knew how to cover without wooden scaffolding. A goldsmith named Filippo Brunelleschi said he could do it.

He did. The dome was finished in 1436, and Europe's imagination went off like a firework.

Italian cities like Florence, Venice and Milan had grown rich on trade and banking, even after the Black Death. The Medici family ran Europe's top bank and ruled Florence from 1434 under Cosimo de' Medici.

Rich families paid for art to show off. Competition between cities pushed artists to outdo each other.

Scholars like Petrarch (1304-1374) hunted for lost Latin texts and admired ancient Rome. This 'humanism' put human achievement at the centre. After 1453, Greek scholars from Constantinople brought more old books to Italy.

The word rinascita (rebirth) was used by the artist-writer Vasari in the 1500s. The word 'Renaissance' was popularised by historian Jacob Burckhardt in 1860.

Leonardo da Vinci (1452-1519) painted the Mona Lisa and filled notebooks with machines and anatomy. Michelangelo carved David and painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling (1508-12), lying on scaffolding, according to traditional accounts, and standing is closer to the truth. Raphael painted The School of Athens around 1509-11.

Niccolo Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513, published after his death in 1532. He said a ruler must deal with the world as it is, not as it should be. People called its advice ruthless. Others read it as an honest study of power.

He has given us the word 'Machiavellian'.

Ideas moved north with the printing press. Erasmus of Rotterdam, Thomas More and later Shakespeare drew on Renaissance humanism. Perspective, anatomy and realism changed painting everywhere.

Other people were left out: women artists were few, though some, like Sofonisba Anguissola, did get fame.

cards.h: Was it really a break with the Middle Ages?
cards.b:
Burckhardt saw it as the birth of the modern individual. Many historians now say medieval Europe was not 'dark': universities, cathedrals and science thrived. Renaissance ideas had medieval roots.

Also, a common myth says medieval people thought the Earth was flat. Educated people knew it was round, and that includes Columbus's critics.
Hampi, Fatehpur Sikri and a Jesuit gift

Five things to remember

  1. Florence's wealth and the Medici paid for art.
  2. Humanism revived classical learning.
  3. Brunelleschi's dome was finished in 1436.
  4. Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513.
  5. Historians question the neat 'break' with the Middle Ages.

Think about it

  • Does art flourish with rich patrons or despite them?
  • Is Machiavelli a cynic or a realist?
